subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Turbo Lag and Solutions
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Turbo Lag and Solutions.

hook.text: Press the throttle on an old turbo car and nothing happens for a moment—then power hits like a wall.

buildup.text: Turbo lag happens because exhaust needs time to spin the turbine up to full speed.

discovery.text: Twin-scroll turbos split exhaust pulses into two channels, spooling the turbine faster.

twist.text: Variable-geometry turbos change blade angles to stay responsive at low speeds and powerful up top.

climax.text: Electric turbos eliminate lag entirely by spinning the compressor with a motor on demand.

punchline.text: Engineers spent decades eliminating that awkward power pause.

quiz.question: What causes turbo lag?
options: Time for exhaust to spin the turbine

details.summary: Turbo lag is the delay between pressing the accelerator and feeling boost pressure build, caused by the time needed for exhaust gases to spin the turbine up to speed, and engineers have developed multiple solutions.
details.whyItMatters: Turbo lag was historically the biggest complaint about turbocharged engines. Solving it has been critical to making turbo engines feel responsive enough to replace larger naturally aspirated engines.
takeaways: Lag occurs because the turbine must reach operating speed from exhaust flow
Twin-scroll turbos separate exhaust pulses for faster spool-up
Electric turbochargers eliminate lag by motor-spinning the compressor

faq.question: What is an electric turbocharger?
faq.answer: An electric motor directly spins the compressor wheel to provide instant boost before exhaust flow reaches the turbine. Mercedes-AMG's new inline-six uses this technology to eliminate lag while maintaining high-RPM turbine efficiency.

faq.question: How do twin-turbo setups reduce lag?
faq.answer: Sequential twin-turbo systems use a small turbo for quick low-RPM response and a larger turbo for high-RPM power. Parallel setups use two smaller turbos that spool faster than one large one would.
